questions.stem: Arrange the sequence of the event of the cell cycles:Cyclin D-CDK4Cyclin A-CDK1Cyclin B-CDK1Cyclin E-CDK2Select the correct answer using the code below:
questions.solutionHtml:
1 → 4 → 2 → 3
  • Cyclins are named such because they undergo a constant cycle of synthesis and degradation during cell division.
  • When cyclins are synthesized, they act as an activating protein and bind to CDKs forming a Cyclin-CDK complex.
  • This complex then acts as a signal to the cell to pass to the next cell cycle phase.

CELL CYCLE:

  • G0→ G1→ S→ G2→ M
  • 1st step / ON-OFF SWITCH in cell cycle – Phosphorylation of Rb gene.
  • Normally, Rb gene is active in hypophosphorylated state.
  • As Rb gene is a tumour suppressor gene, it binds to E2F (Elongation factor) and inhibits transcription of genes whose products are required for Synthetic (S) phase of cell cycle.
  • Phosphorylation of Rb gene leads to release of E2F and leads to transcription of genes whose products are required for Synthetic (S) phase of cell cycle.
  • Cyclins and Cyclin dependent kinases are involved in cell cycle.

Cyclin D, Cyclin E, Cyclin A and Cyclin B gets activated sequentially and binds to Cyclin Dependent inhibitors - CDK 4 , CDK2, CDK1 and CDK 1 respectively and completes the cell cycle. 

Role of cyclins, cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs) and CDK inhibitors (CDKIs) in regulating the cell cycle. Shaded arrows represent the phases of the cell cycle during which specific Cyclin-CDK complexes are active.

  • Cyclin D-CDK4, Cyclin D-CDK6, and Cyclin E-CDK2 regulate the G1 -to-S transition by phosphorylating the Rb protein (pRb).
  • Cyclin A-CDK2 and Cyclin A-CDK1 are active in the S phase.
  • Cyclin B-CDK1 is essential for the G2 -to-M transition.
  • Two families of CDK inhibitors can block activity of CDKs and progression through the cell cycle. The so-called INK4 inhibitors, composed of p15, p16, p18, and p19, act on cyclin D-CDK4 and cyclin D-CDK6.
  • The other family of three inhibitors, p21, p27, and p57, can inhibit all CDKs.

CELL CYCLE INHIBITORS

Cip/Kip Family :

  • Includes p21, p27 and p57.
  • These can bind to Cyclin-CDK and inactivate them

INK4/ARF Family:

  • Includes p16INK4a and p14 ARF
  • p16INK4a inhibits CDK4
  • p14 ARF prevents p53 degradation by inhibiting MDM2

CELL CYCLE CHECKPOINTS:

  • G1/S and G2/M checkpoints.
  • Cell damage caused by Ionising Radiation arrests the cells at G2/M checkpoint
  • After cell cycle arrest at different points, the cell has to activate the DNA repair mechanisms and repair itself and if not, apoptosis has to happen rendering the cell to die.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best indicator to assess iron deficiency anemia:

options.label: A
options.text: TIBS increased, Ferritin increased, Transferrin saturation increased, Serum transferrin receptors increased

options.label: B
options.text: TIBS reduced, Ferritin reduced, Transferrin saturation reduced, Serum transferrin receptors decreased

options.label: C
options.text: TIBS increased, Ferritin reduced, Transferrin saturation reduced, Serum transferrin receptors decreased

options.label: D
options.text: TIBS increased, Ferritin reduced, Transferrin saturation reduced, Serum transferrin receptors increased

questions.answerText: TIBS increased, Ferritin reduced, Transferrin saturation reduced, Serum transferrin receptors increased
questions.solutionHtml:
TIBS increased, Ferritin reduced, Transferrin saturation reduced, Serum transferrin receptors increased
  • In Iron Deficiency Anemia (IDA), TIBC (Total iron-binding capacity) is increased, transferrin saturation is decreased, and ferritin is decreased.
  • The diagnosis of IDA ultimately rests on laboratory studies.
  • Serum Fe and ferritin are low and the Total plasma Fe binding capacity is high. Low serum Fe with increased Fe binding capacity results in a reduction of transferrin saturation to below 15%.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 655-658

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following conditions is shown below?
questions.solutionHtml:
Plexiform neurofibroma
  • The given image shows Plexiform neurofibroma.
  • It is a characteristic feature of neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1), also known as von Recklinghausen disease.
  • It is a genetic disorder characterized by the development of benign tumors called neurofibromas in the peripheral nervous system.
  • Plexiform neurofibromas specifically involve multiple nerve fascicles and can infiltrate and expand along the nerve structures.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Chapter 23

Acute Respiratory infection
  • Ciliocytophthoria (CCP) defines a degenerative process of the ciliated cells consequent to viral infections, and it is characterized by typical morphological changes.
  • It can occur in various conditions affecting the respiratory tract, including acute respiratory infections such as viral or bacterial respiratory tract infections.
  • During respiratory infections, the ciliated respiratory epithelial cells lining the airways may become damaged or shed, leading to their presence in respiratory specimens.
  • The presence of ciliocytophthoria in sputum or other respiratory samples is often indicative of ongoing respiratory epithelial cell damage or turnover.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Chapter 13

questions.stem: Which of the following is not small round cell?
questions.solutionHtml:
Hemangioblastoma
  • Hemangioblastoma is not a small round blue cell tumor
  • Hemangioblastoma are tumors of CNS that originate from vascular tissues. They demonstrate the proliferation of capillaries with variable sized, closely packed, and thin walled vessels.

questions.stem: Which of the following regarding BM biopsy needle and for the procedure is not true:

options.label: A
options.text: Can be done in a prone or lateral position

options.label: B
options.text: To find out infiltrative and granulomatous disorders

options.label: D
options.text: Platelet count of 40000 is a contraindication

questions.answerText: Platelet count of 40000 is a contraindication
questions.solutionHtml:
Platelet count of 40000 is a contraindication

In Bone marrow biopsy, most of the situations where bone marrow aspiration is indicated (eg suspected Acute Leukaemia, bone marrow infiltrative disorders), thrombocytopenia is usually present; So, a platelet count of < 40,000/micro L is not a contraindication to bone marrow aspiration.
